order_note: No predecessor and no order on this engine. SQL 137 (security audit 2026-10-29, finding 15, medium, database access only) needs public.identity_accounts (application_user_id, email, status) with its unique index identity_accounts_email_lower_key on lower(email) (aws/identity/sql/01_identity_accounts.sql), public.profiles (id, email), auth.uid(), public.is_platform_owner() (aws/rls/sql/10_owner_helpers_from_identity.sql, no later migration redefines it) owned by checksops_admin, and the roles checksops and authenticated; the file itself raises sql137_table_missing, sql137_column_missing, sql137_function_missing, sql137_role_missing or sql137_owner_email_not_unique otherwise. It also refuses unless exactly one identity_accounts row in status active or isolated_test carries checksopsadmin@gmail.com (sql137_owner_identity_count) and no profiles row carries that mailbox without that identity row (sql137_owner_profile_without_identity), so every user is_platform_owner() recognizes before the file is recognized after it. Those two row checks run inside the file, not in the read-only inspect (which reads no table rows): an apply that meets them fails closed and rolls back. Today is_platform_owner() is true when the caller's identity_accounts row OR its profiles row carries the mailbox, and checksops holds table-level UPDATE on profiles (SQL 66, aws/identity/sql/07) and, where aws/identity/sql/07 ran, on identity_accounts: a session holding the checksops credentials could make any user the platform owner by rewriting an email. SQL 137 keeps only the identity branch (same mailbox, same row: the owner is identified exactly as today) and revokes UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE on identity_accounts from PUBLIC, anon, authenticated and checksops. No API path updates either email column or updates, deletes or truncates identity_accounts (aws/functions/api: profiles UPDATEs set only full_name, phone and totp_enrolled_at; identity_accounts is inserted with ON CONFLICT (cognito_sub) DO NOTHING); the invite function (SQL 90 / SQL 101) writes identity_accounts as its SECURITY DEFINER owner and is not affected. profiles' grants are not changed (its email no longer decides is_platform_owner()); is_master_owner() delegates and is not changed. If the read-only inspect finds the function already identity-only with the pinned EXECUTE ACL and none of the revoked lines it reports already_applied true and nothing is applied (the pin is then recorded as verified live, not applied).

tooling.note: Guarded tooling for SQL 137: sql137-platform-owner-identity-production-apply.mjs --inspect (read-only) and the receipt-gated --apply on the engine shared with the staging guarded executor (choice sql137-platform-owner-identity); production-sql-one-shot.mjs --migration sql137. intended_replacement_sha256 is the code-derived fingerprint (releaseIntendedHash in release-sql-state.mjs, equal to the staging pin's): public.is_platform_owner() as the file leaves it (LANGUAGE sql, STABLE, SECURITY DEFINER, result boolean, proconfig row_security=off and search_path=public, the identity-only body, EXECUTE authenticated, checksops and the owner) and the UPDATE / DELETE / TRUNCATE lines of PUBLIC, anon, authenticated and checksops on public.identity_accounts, which must be none (spec table_privileges, as SQL 106). The pre-conditions refuse any other live EXECUTE grant on the function than the kept ones and PUBLIC, anon and service_role (function_acl_replaceable); every other grant on identity_accounts (SELECT, INSERT, the owner's) must be unchanged (other_table_privileges_unchanged), and every other object, column ACL included, is in the unrelated-catalog snapshot. The tooling does not authorize anything: this pin stays execute false until a reviewed change records the staging acceptance, the production inspect and an owner approval.
